    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">We're prioritising investigations into rebates, discounts and payments that see suppliers pay around $6 billion to the major supermarkets every year.
 
These payments effectively reduce the final price the major supermarkets pay suppliers and are not usually available to other retailers.
 
The impact is that it becomes much harder for other retailers to get their foot in the door and compete, reinforcing a market structure where a few big players hold the majority of the market.
 
There are over 50 different types of payments the major supermarkets could charge suppliers for, including shelf restocking, promotional support, aisle cleaning and other in-store services.
 
We'll be making sure the major supermarkets are following the rules set out in grocery competition law when charging these payments.         " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">Severe weather and growing pressure on critical infrastructure are making disruptions to electricity, water, and telecommunications more frequent and visible – and ultimately more costly for communities.

We also know that improving the resilience of the infrastructure New Zealanders rely on every day is likely to require additional investment. 
Because consumers ultimately bear both the costs – and the benefits – of these investments, it's critical that investment is carefully assessed, clearly justified, and grounded in what matters most to communities.

Today, the Commerce Commission released draft cross-sector guidance to support a more structured, transparent, and community-informed approach to resilience investment.

We’re seeking feedback and welcome engagement from infrastructure providers, stakeholders, and communities.
Submissions are open to 31 July 2026.
